Leor sent an attachment.
The team's never practiced, that's what you loved about it so much. You just had a game every Saturday night where you got to hang out with your friends and have a mildly competitive game with the other team. The small sports complex was behind the Carnation City Mall, the one that was closing to be demolished, the one you spent your childhood in. It was mid-november and the snow occasionally puddled up in the parking lot, getting your shoes soaking wet when you stepped out of the car. The contrast from the freezing night to the warm inside of the complex felt strange. The inside had this hard to describe smell; like when you press your nose up to a thick sweater and breathe in, rubbery, dusty, and stale. The games were fun besides getting slammed up on the walls occasionally or shredding parts of your shins and knees if you fell down on the turf. Your soccer league was coached and funded by a man who ran a hot dog cart for the homecoming fair and he named the team the Minerva monsters, but you all called yourselves the "Minerva Glizzys" instead, and before each game started you would put you hands in a circle and yell "1, 2, 3, Glizzys!" After each game, you'd ride home with your friend, sitting in the back of his minivan. His mom would always stop at the Little Caesars Pizza and buy the $5 Hot N Ready for you to eat on the way back home. You looked forward to that every Saturday night. As Christmas inched closer the season ended and the mall was demolished shortly after. The sports complex is still there and used, but that would be the last time you played there. . . . . . #suburbanobituary #nostalgia #nostalgic #memory #memories #forgotten #forgottenplaces #suburbs #suburban #liminal #liminalspaces #2000s #midwest #2000skids #indoorsoccer #alliance #ohio #smalltown

Daniel Naroditsky (November 9, 1995 – October 19, 2025) was an American chess grandmaster, author, commentator, and educator who died unexpectedly at the age of 29. He was a prominent and popular figure in the chess world, known for his insightful commentary, educational content, and engaging livestreams under the nickname "Danya".  Career and Achievements Grandmaster Title: Naroditsky earned the prestigious Grandmaster title, the highest in chess apart from World Champion, in 2013 at the age of 18. Junior Success: He was a child prodigy who won the Under-12 section of the World Youth Chess Championship in 2007 and the U.S. Junior Championship in 2013. Author and Educator: At just 14 years old, he published a book titled Mastering Positional Chess: Practical Lessons from a Junior World Champion. He later became a respected coach at the Charlotte Chess Center and had a large online following through his YouTube and Twitch channels. FIDE Rating: As of October 2025, his FIDE standard rating was 2619. He also excelled at blitz chess and was consistently ranked in the world's top 25 blitz players. Stanford Graduate: Naroditsky graduated from Stanford University with a bachelor's degree in history in 2019.  Passing Naroditsky passed away unexpectedly on October 19, 2025, just two weeks before his 30th birthday. His family announced the death in a statement released by the Charlotte Chess Center, asking for privacy. Stanford University tops the list of the best U.S. colleges in the latest WSJ/College Pulse rankings.⁠ ⁠ Unlike other school rankings, this list emphasizes one point: How well did the college prepare students for financial success? More than any other factor, it rewards the boost an institution provides to its graduates’ salaries, beyond an estimate of what they could have expected from attending any college.⁠ ⁠ Stanford returns to the top of this list for the first time since the 2017 rankings. Ivy League schools also figure prominently, with Yale University, Princeton University and Harvard University finishing third, fourth and fifth, respectively. Two other Ivy League schools—Columbia University and the University of Pennsylvania—come in at eighth and ninth, respectively.⁠ ⁠ Beyond the marquee names, the rankings’ distinct methodology highlights some institutions that don’t have as much name recognition but still help their students achieve remarkable success.⁠ ⁠ Babson College—the small Wellesley, Mass., school focused on business and entrepreneurship—retained its No. 2 spot from last year. Claremont McKenna College, near Los Angeles, clocked in at No. 6, and Davidson College, near Charlotte, N.C., ranked 10th.⁠ ⁠ A lot of things have remained constant from last year. Eighteen of the top 20 schools are the same, with a wide variety of colleges, including large public schools, small private schools, technology institutes and liberal-arts colleges in this upper tier.⁠ ⁠ In addition to graduates’ salaries, the rankings consider schools’ graduation rates and diversity—and their learning environment, based on a survey of about 120,000 students and recent alumni. The survey measured factors such as quality of teaching and feedback, career preparation and learning facilities, and how likely students were to recommend their school to a friend.⁠ ⁠ See the full rankings at the link in our bio.⁠ ⁠ Photo: John G.
